summary: In this tutorial, you learn how to create an inert gas using the Periodic Table tool in the JChemComp environment on Linux version 12.04 and Java version 7.1210. First, open the terminal and navigate to the desktop by typing `cd /home/username/Desktop` and pressing Enter, then type `jchemcomp` and press Enter to open JChemComp. To access the Periodic Table, click the toolbar button or right-click and select "Periodic Table." This opens a window showing the periodic table with elements. Click on an element symbol like 'Y' to view its details in the info box. Close the window by clicking the close button or right-clicking and selecting "Close." To create an inert gas compound, go to the menu, select "Reaction," and click "New Reaction." Place the cursor on the desired element, such as oxygen, and click to add it to the reaction. For example, type "Y" in the text box and click to add yttrium. Then, go to the menu, select "Isotopes," and choose the isotope of yttrium. Click on the atom and change the element to yttrium using the right-click menu. Navigate to the "Properties" section and select "Inert Gases" from the dropdown menu. This will show properties specific to inert gases.
